rows.intake: A Dutch voice walkthrough is transcribed in timed turns, each with a start and an end.
rows.fact_extraction: Facts are read from the form and the walkthrough. Each keeps its source: a form field, or a quote from one turn.
rows.vision_inventory: {photos} photos are read for room and condition, and checked for faces and license plates. None needed blurring.
rows.reconciliation: {conflicts} conflicts surface between the form, the voice, and the photos. A bedroom photo shows carpet where the voice said laminate.
rows.gate1: Build year: the spoken {voice} is kept over the form’s {form}. Owners’ association contribution: the form’s €175 is kept over the spoken €165. Bedroom floor: neither value is kept.
rows.creative: Portal text of {portal} sentences and a social caption of {social}. Each sentence cites the facts it rests on.
rows.qa_cards: {questions} buyer questions, answered in {answers} sentences from the same facts.
rows.staging: One empty room is furnished as a bedroom. The result is labelled “Virtually staged” and shown next to the original.
rows.integrity: Windows, doors, and other fixed elements are counted before and after. All are unchanged, so the staged image is offered.
rows.verification: {audited} sentences are tested against the facts they cite. {flagged} are flagged.
rows.gate2: Nothing is flagged. The staged image is accepted, with its label, and the copy is approved.
rows.export: {files} files are built, among them the HTML pack and the portal fields. Every publication check passes.

numbers.title: The numbers, and their limits
numbers.intro: A seeded-defect evaluation: known problems are planted in synthetic inputs, and we count what the pipeline catches. Recorded {date} in fixture mode (recorded responses, no model calls) on {sets} synthetic sets. Run it yourself with npm run eval.

rows.planted: Planted conflicts surfaced at the first review
rows.injectedFlagged: Injected claim defects flagged in the first audit
rows.injectedAtGate2: Injected defects still unflagged at the second review
rows.injectedExported: Injected defects in an exported pack

limits.blatant: The planted defects are blatant. The numbers show that the checks catch such text, not how often the writing model produces it.
limits.oneApartment: All six sets are variations of one synthetic apartment. This is evidence that the mechanism works, not a catch rate for real listings.
limits.freeform: Conflicts about free-form details, such as a floor material, are found by the model on a best-effort basis. Only market facts are guaranteed by code.
limits.audio: The audit checks sentences against the facts and their quotes, not against the audio. In the sample file the walkthrough script says “L-vormige” (L-shaped), the transcript says “ellipsvormige”, and the copy says “elliptical”. The second review is where you would catch it.

items.valuation: Value a property or give investment advice.
items.legal: Interpret law, draft contracts, or advise on title. The publication checklist helps you spot missing items; it does not certify legal compliance.
items.buyers: Screen, score, or rank buyers or tenants.
items.publishing: Publish to a portal for you. You download the pack and decide where it goes.
items.edits: Edit a photo to hide a defect or change the structure. Staging adds furniture; if a window, door, or radiator changes, the original is used instead.
items.metadata: Keep GPS or other photo metadata. It is stripped from every photo at upload.
items.blur: Export a face or a license plate. Both are blurred in exported photos.
items.deletion: Keep a project you delete. Deleting removes its photos, voice memo, facts, and pack for good.
